title: A prose block over 200 KB silently shows raw Markdown source instead of rendered output, with no cue to the user
file: src/worker/md.ts (maxHtmlChars, DEFAULT_RENDER_OPTIONS in src/shared/types.ts) + src/preview/createPreview.ts:688-713 (md-plain mounting)
repro: Dev server on :5202, then `node /Users/zyx/LocalDocuments/MDReader/bench/verify/r8-cycle.mjs` — see the 'extreme: 10k inline links in one paragraph' and 'one 200k-char cell' cases; also `node /Users/zyx/LocalDocuments/MDReader/bench/verify/big.mjs` ('1 MB paragraph rendered as raw text'). Minimal repro: load a single paragraph of 10000 `[l0](https://e.com/0)` links (277 KB) via `__mdr.loadText`.
expected: Either the block is rendered (markdown-it renders the same 1 MB paragraph in 82 ms in Node, measured by bench/verify/big.mjs), or the preview tells the user why it is not — the current output is indistinguishable from a rendering bug.
actual: The block is mounted as HTML_FLAG_PLAIN: `a: 0` anchors, `tds: 0` table cells, text length equals the source length, and the visible content is literal `**bold**` / `[text](url)` / `| a | b |` markup. No badge, class-driven hint, toast, or status-bar note explains the downgrade. This is spec-conformant (SPEC §4.4 `maxHtmlChars: 200000`, SPEC §9 failure table), hence low, but it is silent.
suggestedFix: Prefix a PLAIN-mounted block with a small non-selectable notice (e.g. 「此段落超过 200 KB，按原文显示」) using the existing `.md-plain` wrapper, or raise `maxHtmlChars` for Prose blocks now that the measured render cost is ~80 ms/MB.

title: Setext `## ` heading whose text contains `|` is classified Table → missing from outline, TOC and export heading ids
repro:
Unit: `cd /Users/zyx/LocalDocuments/MDReader && npx vitest run test/review-outline-kind.test.ts` (3 assertions fail).
Browser: `npx vite --port 5205 --strictPort &` then `node bench/verify/review-misc.mjs` — checks "A: TOC lists every rendered <h2>" and "A: export gives every <h2> an id".
Minimal document:
```
配置项 | 说明
---

正文。

普通标题
---
```
expected:
Both underlined lines are rendered by markdown-it as `

` (verified: `md.render` emits `

配置项 | 说明

` and `

普通标题

`), so both must appear in the outline/TOC (SPEC §4.3.9 "plus 2-line setext blocks") and both must get an `id=` in the exported HTML so `#anchor` links resolve.
actual: `kindOf` runs its Table test (`first line contains '|' && next line matches TABLE_DELIM`) after every other kind test, so `配置项 | 说明` + `---` becomes `BlockKind.Table` (asserted in the test). `updateOutline` then skips the block outright (`kind !== Heading && (lineCount < 2 || (kind !== Prose && kind !== Html))`), and `setextHeadings` would bail anyway (`b.kind !== Prose`). Observed in the browser: preview `<h2>` = ["配置项 | 说明", "普通标题"], TOC = ["普通标题"]; exported HTML contains 2 `<h2>` but only 1 `id` (["普通标题"]), so the in-document link `[去配置项](#配置项--说明)` is dead both live and in the export. Block height is also estimated with the Table formula (36 px/line) instead of 28.
suggestedFix: Make the Table branch match GFM's actual rule instead of "delimiter row looks like dashes": only return `Table` when the delimiter row's cell count equals the header row's (split both on `|` after stripping one optional leading and trailing pipe). `配置项 | 说明` (2 cells) vs `---` (1 cell) then falls through to `Prose`, and the existing setext path in `setextHeadings`/`computeHeads` produces the outline entry with no other change. `| a |` + `---` (1 vs 1) stays a Table, matching markdown-it. If you prefer to keep `kindOf` as-is, the alternative is to let `updateOutline` accept `BlockKind.Table` blocks with `lineCount >= 2` and route them through `setextHeads(lines, { ...b, kind: BlockKind.Prose }, b.startLine - 1)` — but that needs the same cell-count test to avoid emitting a bogus heading for a real 1-column table.

title: AppHandle.dispose() does not undo createLayout and never disposes the TOC — the shell, its listeners and its rAF chain stay alive; a second createApp duplicates the whole UI
file: /Users/zyx/LocalDocuments/MDReader/src/app/App.ts:730 (dispose) and /Users/zyx/LocalDocuments/MDReader/src/preview/toc.ts:34 (createToc has no teardown at all)
repro: `cd /Users/zyx/LocalDocuments/MDReader && npx vite --port 5205 --strictPort &` then `node bench/verify/review-misc.mjs` — checks "B: dispose() removes the layout it created" and "B: createApp after dispose does not duplicate the shell". The script loads small.md, counts the shell elements under `#app`, calls `window.__mdr.app.dispose()`, recounts, then `import('/src/app/App.ts').createApp(root)` and counts again.
expected: `dispose()` releases everything `createApp` created (CONTRACT §1 lists it on AppHandle), so `#app` is left as it was found and re-creating the app into the same root yields exactly one toolbar / main / statusbar / overlay / TOC nav.
actual: After `dispose()`: `{toolbar:1, main:1, statusbar:1, overlay:1, tocNav:1, tocItems:61, gutter:1}` still in the DOM (only `.mdr-preview` is removed, by `preview.dispose()`; `disposeEditor` removes the CM subtree). `createToc` is never disposed: its `nav` click listener stays live, and `buildRaf` (sliced build, up to `SLICE_MAX_ITEMS` per frame) and `revealRaf` are never cancelled — after dispose a sliced build of a large outline keeps scheduling rAFs and appending anchors. Re-creating: `{toolbar:2, main:2, statusbar:2, overlay:2, tocNav:2}`. `installSplitResize`'s returned disposer also leaves its pending `requestAnimationFrame(apply)` uncancelled (layout.ts:79/117).
suggestedFix:
1) Give `createLayout` a teardown (return it alongside `els`, or have App keep the four created nodes) and call it at the end of `App.dispose()` — e.g. `toolbar.remove(); main.remove(); statusbar.remove(); overlay.remove(); root.classList.remove('mdr-app'); delete root.dataset.mode; delete root.dataset.toc;`.
2) Add a `dispose()` to `createToc` reached through a WeakMap side table (the same pattern already used by `disposeToolbar` / `disposePalette` / `disposeTheme`, since `TocApi` is frozen): `cancelBuild(); if (revealRaf) cancelAnimationFrame(revealRaf); nav.removeEventListener('click', onClick); nav.remove();` and call it from `App.dispose()`.
3) In `installSplitResize`'s disposer add `if (frame) cancelAnimationFrame(frame);`.

title: isToWorker is a type-only guard, so a well-typed but malformed worker message throws inside the render core (or silently poisons the viewport) instead of being ignored as the code claims
repro: `cd /Users/zyx/LocalDocuments/MDReader && npx vitest run test/review-worker-guards.test.ts` — the `BUG:` assertion fails and prints the four throwing messages.
expected: render.worker.ts:7-8 states the intent verbatim: "anything that is not a ToWorker message (a stray postMessage from an extension or a port handshake) is ignored instead of throwing inside the core". Malformed payloads should be dropped.
actual: `isToWorker` only checks `typeof x === 'object' && FROM/TO_WORKER_TYPES.has(x.type)`, so it returns true for `{type:'edit'}`, `{type:'need'}`, `{type:'setDoc',docId,version}`, `{type:'viewport'}`, `{type:'draft'}`. `core.handle` then throws: `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')` (edit), `m.ids is not iterable` (need), `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'indexOf')` (setDoc), `draft[m.action] is not a function` (draft). An exception in the worker's `onmessage` surfaces as a worker `error` event, which `workerClient` treats as a crash and answers with a full restart + 「渲染器已重启」 toast. `{type:'viewport'}` does not throw but sets `viewport = {firstLine: undefined, lastLine: undefined}`, making `updateWindow`'s `win.first/last` NaN so `inWindow()` is false for every block and the auto-push window silently dies until the next real viewport message. Note `draft[m.action]()` is also an unguarded property lookup on an object literal, so `{type:'draft', action:'constructor'}` is callable.
suggestedFix: Validate the payload in `isToWorker` (per type: `Array.isArray(changes)` with numeric from/to and string insert, `Array.isArray(ids)`, `typeof text === 'string'`, `Number.isFinite(firstLine) && Number.isFinite(lastLine)`, `action` in a literal Set, `typeof requestId === 'number'`), and/or wrap the dispatch in render.worker.ts: `try { core.handle(e.data) } catch (err) { ctx.postMessage({ type:'error', message: String(err), fatal:false }) }`. Replace `draft[m.action]()` in core.ts:371 with an explicit switch.

title: Dead exports and duplicated slug logic
repro: `cd /Users/zyx/LocalDocuments/MDReader && grep -rn 'isRefDefinition\|__setMathState' src/ test/ bench/` → only the definitions. `grep -rn 'queue.clear()\|\.clear()' src/preview/` → `MountQueue.clear` has no caller in src/, test/ or bench/. `grep -n visible src/editor/createEditor.ts` → assigned at :256, never read except on the next line.
expected: No unreferenced exported API surface; one implementation of the heading-slug rule.
actual: `segmenter.isRefDefinition` (exported, zero callers anywhere), `math.__setMathState` (documented as a test hook, zero callers — so the KaTeX-failure path has no test), `MAX_TEX_CHARS` exported but only used inside math.ts, `MountQueue.clear()` (zero callers; `dispose()` is the only path used). `createEditor.ts:99 let visible = true` is written by `setVisible` and immediately re-read on the same line — `if (on) view.requestMeasure()` is equivalent, the variable carries no state. Separately, the heading-slug rule exists twice: `slugify` in `src/worker/outline.ts:63` (no `.trim()`) and `src/preview/interactions.ts:15` (with `.trim()`); `resolveAnchor` depends on the two staying byte-identical, and the module-ownership rule (SPEC §2: only App.ts imports across directories) means nothing enforces that.
suggestedFix: Delete `isRefDefinition`, `MountQueue.clear`, the `visible` variable, and either delete `__setMathState` or add the KaTeX-failure test it was written for (`math=false` + one 「公式渲染不可用」 error message, SPEC §9); un-export `MAX_TEX_CHARS`. For the slug rule, move `slugify` into `src/shared/` (both modules already import from `src/shared/*`, so it does not break the ownership rule) — that is the only change that makes the preview's anchor resolution provably match the worker's slugs.

title: Heading commands (Mod-1..6) stack the ATX marker in front of an existing list/quote marker, producing broken headings
repro: cd /Users/zyx/LocalDocuments/MDReader && npx vite --port 5203 --strictPort &  then  node bench/verify/fx/22-hazards.mjs  (step "heading command on a list line produces sane markdown"). Manually: load `- 项目一`, put the cursor in the line, press Meta+1. Also load `> 引用一`, cursor in line, press Meta+2.
expected: The heading marker is applied to the line's content, after (or instead of) the existing block prefix — e.g. `# 项目一` (or `- # 项目一`), and `> ## 引用一`. setHeading already has `listMarkerWidth()` and `quotePrefixLength()` helpers in the same file (used by indentListItem/dedentListItem) that give the correct insertion offset.
actual:
`- 项目一` + Meta+1 -> `# - 项目一`, which the preview renders as `

- 项目一

` — the literal `- ` becomes part of the heading text and of the TOC entry. `> 引用一` + Meta+2 -> `## > 引用一` (renders as a heading whose text starts with `>`; the blockquote is destroyed). setHeading() inserts at `line.from` unconditionally, only looking at HEADING_RE.
suggestedFix: In setHeading(), compute the insertion offset as quotePrefixLength(line.text) plus (for list lines) listMarkerWidth(), the same way indentListItem does, and apply HEADING_RE to the remainder; decide deliberately whether a list item becomes `- # x` or loses its marker, but never emit `# - x`.

title: P13: renderer memory on huge.md peaks at 1.45 GB while typing (target < 450 MB) — a full-document Int32Array/Float64Array is reallocated on every keystroke
file: src/worker/core.ts:188 (postStructure allocates new Int32Array(blocks.length * BLOCK_STRIDE) per edit); src/preview/createPreview.ts:484 + src/preview/heights.ts:54 (new Float64Array(nNew) heights + tops per applyStructure)
repro: cd /Users/zyx/LocalDocuments/MDReader && npx vite --port 5201 --strictPort &  then: node bench/verify/p13-huge-settled.mjs huge 60   (also node bench/verify/p13-typing-growth.mjs huge 6 100 100, node bench/verify/p13-step-attrib.mjs huge split, and node bench/verify/p13-worker-traffic.mjs huge 10 200 for the per-edit byte counts). Flow = open /test-data/huge.md (6.6 MB, 340k lines) in split mode, wait mdr:idle, gotoLine(~170003), type 600 chars at 100 ms, wheel+scroll to end, sample the renderer process footprint via browser CDP SystemInfo.getProcessInfo + macOS `footprint`.
expected: SPEC §11 P13: renderer process < 450 MB after load + 1 min typing + scroll to end.
actual: huge.md: 577 MB after load alone, 1447 MB peak right after the 60 s typing phase, 1149 MB after scroll-to-end, and it only falls back to 457 MB after a 30 s idle + forced GC — still over target. Reproducible: separate runs measured 1283 MB, 1313 MB, 1204 MB during/after typing. Per-keystroke breakdown (bench/verify/p13-worker-traffic.mjs): each edit changes exactly 1 block but the worker still posts a fresh 1.53 MB Int32Array (100002 blocks x 4 ints) and the preview allocates a fresh 0.8 MB heights Float64Array + 0.8 MB tops array, i.e. ~3.1 MB of new buffers per keystroke; 600 keystrokes = ~1.9 GB of churn, matching the observed 577 -> 1447 MB growth. Page JS heap stays flat (22.1 -> 24.2 MB), so this is external/ArrayBuffer memory that V8 does not reclaim under sustained typing. large.md (3 MB, 102k lines, the fixture the target is written for) passes at 365 MB (0.48 MB per edit), so the problem only appears once the per-edit structure array gets big.
suggestedFix: Stop rebuilding and transferring the whole structure array on every edit. Either (a) send an incremental structure delta (the reconcile in applyStructure already only needs the prefix/suffix boundary + the replaced range), or (b) keep one Int32Array per side and post only {firstChangedIndex, removedCount, insertedBlocks} plus a running lineDelta, or (c) at minimum pool/reuse the buffers: transfer the array back from the main thread after applyStructure and reuse it in postStructure, and grow `heights`/`topsArr` in place instead of allocating a new Float64Array each time.

title: Typing on huge.md re-mounts unchanged neighbouring blocks: 1 block changes per edit but ~9 HTML items are pushed per keystroke
file: src/worker/core.ts:520-533 (produce(): returns an item whenever inWindow(b), regardless of whether the block changed) and src/worker/core.ts:570 (walkNext(walkFill, miss) background back-fill re-picks cache-evicted in-window blocks after every edit)
repro: cd /Users/zyx/LocalDocuments/MDReader && npx vite --port 5201 --strictPort &  then: node bench/verify/arch-mutations.mjs huge 200 100   (and node bench/verify/arch-mutations.mjs large 200 100 for the passing control; node bench/verify/p13-worker-traffic.mjs huge 10 200 for the message counts). The script puts a MutationObserver on .mdr-preview__body, types 200 chars at line ~170003 and classifies every childList mutation by block id and by whether nodes were removed (a re-mount) or only added (a first-time window mount).
expected: A keystroke in a paragraph replaces the children of exactly one .md-block and touches no other block (SPEC §5.2/§4.5: `changed` is the only dirty set; other blocks keep their DOM).
actual: huge.md: 236 childList mutations for 200 keystrokes — 200 direct replaceChildren on the edited block 50002 (correct) plus 36 CONTENT REPLACEMENTS (removedNodes > 0, i.e. already-mounted blocks re-mounted) on unchanged neighbours 49993, 49995, 49997, 49998, 50001, 50003, 50005, 50007, 50008, 50011. Worker traffic for the same scenario: 10 keystrokes -> 10 structure messages with `changed.length === 1` each, but 90 html items (9 blocks re-rendered and pushed per keystroke). large.md is clean: 200 mutations, 200 on the edited block, 0 on other blocks, 1 html item per keystroke. No .md-block wrapper was ever inserted or removed and the edited wrapper kept its element identity on both documents, so the position-stable-id part of the architecture holds.
suggestedFix: In produce(), only return an HtmlItem when the block is actually in `need` or in `dirty` for this version; a block picked by the background cache back-fill (walkFill/miss) should warm the cache and not be pushed to the preview. Alternatively have the preview drop an incoming HtmlItem whose id is already mounted and not in the last `changed` set (mountQueue already has the id, so the check is O(1)).

title: P5: main-thread busy time per keystroke is 15-17 ms p95 at 60 wpm (target < 5 ms) when every task in the keystroke window is counted
file: bench/perf.spec.ts / docs/SPEC.md §11 P5 (metric definition) — no single src/ file is at fault; the marginal cost is within budget
repro: cd /Users/zyx/LocalDocuments/MDReader && npx vite --port 5201 --strictPort &  then: node bench/verify/p5-trace.mjs large 120 100 (Chromium trace, sums de-duplicated renderer RunTask intervals per keystroke window), node bench/verify/p5-clean.mjs large 200 100 split (MessageChannel monitor with an idle baseline), node bench/verify/p5-idle-trace.mjs large 8 (control), node bench/verify/p5-marginal.mjs large 150 (same metric at 100/50/30/15/8 ms spacing), node bench/verify/p5-burst.mjs large 200 15.
expected: SPEC §11 P5: main-thread work per keystroke p95 < 5 ms, max < 10 ms (SPEC §10 budgets 2-5 ms).
actual: Trace-based total main-thread busy in the 100 ms after each key: p50 9.4, p95 15.2-16.9, max 21.0-22.8 ms; the idle control on the same page measures p95 2.6 ms per 100 ms window, so the time is real and keystroke-attributable. However it is NOT an MDReader scaling problem: (1) the same measurement gives 9.6 ms p50 on small.md (31 KB) and 10.1 ms on medium.md, i.e. it is flat in document size; (2) it is identical with the preview hidden (mode=edit: 10.4 ms p50 vs 11.1 ms in split), so the preview/worker path contributes almost nothing; (3) the breakdown is ~5 ms JS (FunctionCall 3.4 + microtasks 0.9; view.dispatch itself is only 0.3-0.6 ms p50 and mount 0.3 ms) and ~5 ms browser rendering (Layout 2.1, UpdateLayoutTree 0.7, Paint 0.7, Layerize 0.5, Commit 0.4) of the CodeMirror viewport; (4) the marginal cost converges to 3.9 ms/key at 15 ms spacing and 2.9 ms/key at 8 ms spacing, i.e. under target, because the fixed per-frame rendering is amortised; (5) the longest single main-thread task per keystroke is 7.2-7.6 ms max, under the 10 ms max target; (6) there are zero long tasks, zero LoAF entries and zero frames > 20 ms while typing at 10, 33 and 66 keys/s, and keystroke->mount latency p95 is 33.7 ms (target < 40 ms). By contrast undo/redo measured the same way is 4.3 ms p95, so the figure is genuinely typing-specific, not a measurement floor.
suggestedFix: Pin down the P5 metric before wiring it into CI, otherwise the gate fails permanently on a 31 KB file. Recommended: assert (a) longest single main-thread task per keystroke < 10 ms, (b) marginal busy time per keystroke measured in a burst (>= 60 keys/s) < 5 ms, and (c) 0 frames > 20 ms — all of which the implementation meets today — rather than 'sum of every task in the 100 ms after the key', which charges a whole rendering frame to each key when keys are sparse.

title: Worker `edit` handling is O(changes × lines-in-block): one Replace-all inside a large single block stalls the renderer past the 10 s watchdog and restarts it
repro:
Start the dev server (`cd /Users/zyx/LocalDocuments/MDReader && npx vite --port 5204 --strictPort`), then:
1) End-user repro: `node bench/verify/s37_fence_replaceall_repro.mjs` — loads the spec's own pathological document (one 50 000-line ```js fence, SPEC §11 `pathological.md`), presses Mod-F, fills search="tok value" / replace="TOKEN value" and clicks the panel's Replace-all button (50 000 matches). No internal APIs are used.
2) Scaling matrix: `node bench/verify/s36_edit_matrix.mjs` (fresh page per row, prints a table).
3) Cascade into the permanent give-up: `node bench/verify/s34_restart_repro.mjs` (four restarts, then the renderer is dead for the rest of the session).
4) Same root cause via plain typing: `node bench/verify/s38_fence_typing_burst.mjs`.
expected: A Replace-all (a spec'd feature, SPEC §7/§8, CM search panel) on a document class the spec explicitly targets (P6 "5k-line fence", P7 "unclosed ``` at line 1", `pathological.md` "one 50k-line fence") completes without tripping the worker-silence watchdog. SPEC §4.2/§10 budget the worker at 0.2–1 ms of splice+resegment per edit and the preview to update "within 1–2 frames".
actual:
`edit()` applies the changes one at a time and calls `resegmentWindow` after EVERY change (src/worker/core.ts:262-266). Inside one giant block each `resegmentWindow` rescans the whole block, so the cost is O(changes × lines-in-block). Measured cost of a single transaction, time from `view.dispatch` to the worker's `structure` (s36):
  1 000-line block, 1 000 changes → 220 ms (0.22 ms/change)
  5 000-line block, 1 000 changes → 961 ms (0.96 ms/change)
  20 000-line block, 1 000 changes → 3 823 ms (3.82 ms/change)
  50 000-line block, 1 000 changes → 9 507 ms (9.51 ms/change)
  50 000-line block, 5 000 changes → >10 s → WORKER RESTARTED
  control, same 50 000 lines split into 50 000 paragraph blocks, 100 000 changes → 457 ms
In s37 the UI Replace-all produced `[workerClient] restarting render worker: no structure within 10 s` at +10 449 ms and the toast 「渲染器已重启」. In s34, repeating the operation restarted the renderer 4 times, which latches the permanent give-up (see the separate finding) — the preview and the worker-side draft autosave are then dead until a full page reload; `settle()` afterwards times out at 240 s. Plain typing hits the same wall without a restart but with a huge lag: a 1 200-char burst in a 50 000-line fence leaves the preview 12 776 ms behind the last keystroke (s38), vs the P5 target of 40 ms keystroke→mount.
suggestedFix: Do not resegment per change. In `edit()` (src/worker/core.ts:255-282) group the resolved changes into the maximal affected line window (or per containing block) and run `resegmentWindow` once per contiguous region after all the text splices of that region have been applied — `applyResolved` already returns the effect ranges, so they can be merged (reverse order already guarantees earlier changes keep their original coordinates). A cheap interim mitigation is to fall back to `segmentAll` when `changes.length × affectedBlockLines` exceeds a threshold, and to have the worker post an interim `structure` (or a heartbeat) while a long `edit` is in flight so `SILENCE_MS` cannot fire on legitimate work.

title: `gaveUp` in the worker client is a permanent latch, so the documented "≤ 3 restarts per minute" rate limit never reopens
repro: `node bench/verify/s30_giveup_permanent.mjs` (dev server on :5204). It crashes the worker 4 times inside a minute, then types, waits 70 s (past `RESTART_WINDOW_MS = 60_000`), types again and waits another 20 s (past `SILENCE_MS`). Takes ~2 min. Also reproduced as the end state of `node bench/verify/s34_restart_repro.mjs`.
expected: SPEC §8/§9 specify a RATE limit — "max 3 restarts/min" — and `restartTimes` + `RESTART_WINDOW_MS` in the same function implement a sliding window. After the window expires, the next crash or silence should be allowed to restart the renderer again so the app self-heals.
actual: `restart()` begins with `if (disposed || gaveUp) return;` and sets `gaveUp = true` permanently once `restartTimes.length >= MAX_RESTARTS`; the pruned sliding window is never consulted again. Measured: after 4 crashes, `window.__workers.length` stays at 4 forever — 70 s later an edit plus 20 s of silence spawns no worker, `__wmsgs.structure` never advances past 1, and no typed text ever reaches the preview. Consequences observed: (a) the preview is frozen for the rest of the session; (b) the status bar keeps showing 「渲染中 100%」 and stale word/char counts; (c) worker-side draft autosave (SPEC §4.6) stops, so unsaved work has no IndexedDB backup and the user is not told; (d) the 「渲染器多次崩溃，已停止自动重启」 toast carries no action button (only the ×) — the only recovery is a manual page reload, which loses whatever the dead worker never drafted.
suggestedFix: Replace the permanent latch with the sliding window that is already computed: prune `restartTimes` on entry and only refuse a restart while `restartTimes.length >= MAX_RESTARTS` within the last `RESTART_WINDOW_MS` (clear `gaveUp` once the window drains), so a later crash can restart again. Additionally give the fatal toast an action (「重新加载」/「重试渲染器」) and put the status bar into an explicit error state instead of 「渲染中」, and surface that drafts are no longer being saved.

title: `editor.gotoLine` / `editor.scrollToLine` throw a TypeError when the line argument is NaN or undefined
repro: `node bench/verify/s24_api_fuzz_mountall.mjs` — the "API fuzz" section calls every public line-taking editor/preview method with 0, -1, -1e9, 1e9, NaN, Infinity, 1.5, null and undefined.
expected: The public `EditorApi` line-taking methods either clamp or ignore a non-finite argument, like the preview's equivalents do (`preview.blockAtLine`, `lineToScrollTop`, `scrollTopToLine`, `isLineVisible` all survive every value in the fuzz list, and `gotoLine(0 | -1 | 1e9 | null)` is clamped correctly).
actual: 4 throws, all TypeError "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')": `editor.gotoLine(NaN)`, `editor.scrollToLine(NaN)`, `editor.gotoLine(undefined)`, `editor.scrollToLine(undefined)`. `clampLine` (src/editor/createEditor.ts:181) is `Math.min(Math.max(1, Math.floor(line)), view.state.doc.lines)`, which returns NaN for a NaN/undefined input; `view.state.doc.line(NaN)` then yields undefined and `.length` / `.from` throws. Nothing in the current UI feeds NaN in (toc.ts and interactions.ts both guard), so this is an API-robustness nit rather than a user-visible bug — but `nav:gotoLine` is a public bus event any module may emit.
suggestedFix: Make `clampLine` total: `const n = Math.floor(Number(line)); return Number.isFinite(n) ? Math.min(Math.max(1, n), view.state.doc.lines) : 1;` (or have `gotoLine`/`scrollToLine` return early on a non-finite argument).

title: Undoing/applying a very large single transaction blocks the main thread for ~0.2 s (above the 100 ms input-latency budget)
repro: `node bench/verify/s33_search_extremes.mjs` section (B): a 50 000-line document, Replace-all over 100 000 matches from the search panel, then Mod-Z. Latency is measured by the keydown→next-frame probe in `bench/verify/_lib.mjs`. Dispatch cost also measured in `node bench/verify/s35_edit_scaling.mjs` (50 000 paragraph blocks, 100 000 changes).
expected: Input latency (keydown → next animation frame) under 100 ms for any single user gesture; SPEC P12 keeps the longest task under 50 ms.
actual: Undo of the 100 000-change transaction: keydown→frame latency 185.9 ms (wall 186 ms). Applying the same Replace-all: `view.dispatch` alone costs 252.1 ms on the main thread, and a 215 ms long task is recorded. The document result is correct in every case (all 100 000 replacements applied, undo restores the text byte-for-byte, structure tiles, preview matches a from-scratch render), so this is polish, not corruption.
suggestedFix: Flattening the ChangeSet (`flattenChanges`, src/editor/changes.ts:5) and building the `TextChange[]` for a 100 000-change transaction is a measurable part of this; consider transferring very large change sets to the worker in a packed typed-array form (like `packHtml`) instead of an array of objects with `ins.toString()` per change, and/or yielding the postMessage for change sets above a threshold so the frame after the gesture is not blocked.
